messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: P1 alert — GPU driver resets detected in cluster 'prod-usw2-gpu'. Alert shows burst of Xid errors and ECC-corrected spikes on node-gpu-12. Impacting serving-runtime pods in ns=ml-serving. Incident: https://rwinf.example/incident/1802506789

alex: I'm paged, jumping on it. Adding eng-runtime.

maria: I see OOMKills and container restarts for `model-serving-7` and `rtrunner` on node-gpu-12. Heap/training memory looks fine, but kernel log shows repeated GPU resets.

alex: dmesg snippet from node-gpu-12:
```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, Graphics Exception: ...
[ 12345.690123] NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 12345.694321] device nvme0: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector ...
```

maria: also seeing repeated ECC corrected errors in `kern.log` before the reset. Could be thermal/ECC instability.

alex: quick mitigation plan: 1) cordon node-gpu-12, 2) drain non-critical pods, 3) move high-priority customer jobs to warm pool, 4) reboot node and run extended diag, 5) if resets recur, escalate to infra for hardware RMA.

josh: I'll take traffic routing for affected models. Are we failing requests or falling back?

maria: current infra fallback kicked in for HTTP requests -> degraded throughput, some requests returned 503s during pod restarts. Estimated affected QPS ~120 -> ~2.5% of global traffic for those models.

alex: cordoning now: `kubectl cordon node-gpu-12` — marked unschedulable. :white_check_mark:

alex: draining non-daemonset pods, ignoring local data: `kubectl drain node-gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30`

liu: moving canary capacity: scaling up `model-serving-3` in warm-pool (dedicated) to pick up traffic. Running `kubectl scale --replicas=6 deploy/model-serving-3 -n ml-serving`

maria: logs from a crashed container:
```
2026-03-15T12:34:56Z ERROR runtime: GPU reset detected during KV cache write
panic: failed to allocate GPU memory: out of memory
```

alex: NVIDIA driver state: `nvidia-smi -q` shows ECC errors increasing then GPU disappears from list at time of reset.

alex: I'm going to request a soft-reboot of the node (safe reboot) after pods are drained. Infra-Oncall, can you approve a reboot? @infra-oncall

infra-oncall: Approved. Please attach post-reboot diagnostics (nvram logs, lspci, dmesg). If it persists we'll run memtest and schedule vendor support.

alex: Reboot issued: `sudo systemctl reboot`

oncall-bot: Handoff note — alex -> josh at 12:49 UTC. Monitoring for recurrence window (30m) required.

josh: Taking next oncall. Summary: node-gpu-12 had Xid 31/46 spikes, ECC corrected errors, leading to driver resets and pod OOMs. Node cordoned and drained, warm pool scaled, node soft-reboot done. Customer impact: intermittent 503s for ~45 minutes, estimated 3 customer tenants saw degraded latency.

customer-success: Notifying impacted customers with a brief report and ETA for full RCA. Drafted message and sending now.

maria: post-reboot checks — dmesg shows reduced ECC counts but still one Xid 31 at 12:58. GPU was present and `nvidia-smi` returns normal until next Xid. Creating an alternate mitigation: move the node into maintenance (shelf) and replace hardware if Xids continue.

alex: running vendor diagnostics: `sudo /opt/nvidia/bin/nvdiag --extended` and collecting `/var/log/nvidia-installer.log` and `kern.log`. Uploading to incident storage: s3://rwinf-incidents/1802506789/

josh: If we continue to see transient resets, implement soft-fallback policy: route traffic away from the model variant requiring large KV cache allocation and use a smaller quantized model. I'll coordinate rollout.

infra-oncall: Hardware escalation: opening ticket with vendor (NVIDIA) with logs and nvdiag. Ticket ID: NV-64219. They requested kernel logs and systemd-coredump files.

maria: quick note — applying a temporary node taint so autoscaler won't put new pods there: `kubectl taint nodes node-gpu-12 maintenance=drain:NoSchedule`

josh: Monitoring window passing 30m with no further mass resets, but a couple of single Xid events. We're keeping node in maintenance overnight pending vendor advice.

alex: Incident severity -> P1 initially, moving to P2 as customer impact limited by failover. Creating incident ticket and assigning RCA owners (maria + infra-oncall).

oncall-bot: Incident timeline recorded. Next steps: run extended memtest, vendor RMA if Xid > threshold, review firmware/drivers and schedule rolling driver upgrade across GPU pool if needed.

josh: Handoff to overnight oncall (liu). liu — briefing: node-gpu-12 drained & tainted, vendor ticket opened NV-64219, warm-pool scaled, customer-notifications sent. Watch for Xid spikes and GPU disappearances.

liu: Ack, I'm on it. Will check crashloop counts and attach alerts for repeated Xid rate > 5/min. Also will verify auto-eviction thresholds for serving-runtime memory.

maria: adding runbook references: Runbook -> Serving GPU driver resets: https://confluence.rwinf/runbooks/gpu-driver-resets. Follow escalation path and document any firmware changes.

josh: Closing slack thread for active mitigation. If anything significant occurs, reopen thread and re-page. :thumbsup:

alex: Thanks team — good coordination. Will add RCA notes after vendor reply.
